candidates.title: Bay raises $50m to check every AI agent action before it runs: allow, block or ask a person
candidates.summary: Bay, a Tel Aviv startup less than a year old, came out of stealth with $50m (a $37m Series A led by Battery Ventures and a $13m seed led by YL Ventures and Striker Venture Partners; Microsoft's M12 among the investors). Its product reviews each action an AI agent proposes against the whole session and allows it, blocks it or routes it to a person for approval; it names Micron, Peloton, ClickUp and Wix as customers.
candidates.why_it_matters: A mandate checked at the moment of action, not written once and hoped for: the runtime version of reach, mandate and gap, and money flowing into it (after CrowdStrike's buys last week).
claims_to_check: The round and investors at Bay's or Battery Ventures' own announcement
Customer names and the Fortune 100 claim are the company's (TNW notes the latter is unverified)

importance.reason: Agent governance as a funded product, the clearest runtime-mandate design yet; one day old.

candidates.title: OpenAI lets businesses claim ChatGPT profiles and run their own customer agents inside it
candidates.summary: OpenAI launched 'Businesses in ChatGPT' in beta: companies can claim verified profiles, see how often ChatGPT mentions them, and eligible US e-commerce and online-service firms can run their own agent that answers customers from their product data, labelled and kept apart from ChatGPT's answers. Agents must say they are AI, keep prices accurate and avoid pressure tactics; purchases and sharing personal data need the user's explicit approval. Businesses can also sponsor their agent through ChatGPT Ads. The same day OpenAI bought Odessia, a travel agent startup, and shut it down.
candidates.why_it_matters: The platform that hosts the agents writes their mandate: disclosure, accuracy and approval rules set by OpenAI, with ads alongside. A model of agent governance by platform rule rather than by law, worth setting beside Europe's.
claims_to_check: OpenAI's own announcement for the rules and the US-only scope
The Odessia deal: terms undisclosed (reported by TechCrunch and TNW)

importance.reason: A big platform's agent rules, same-day news; US-only for now, far from Portugal.

candidates.title: EU's Digital Fairness Act, due today, would write the first consumer rules for AI shopping agents
candidates.summary: A leaked draft of the Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission is set to present on Wednesday 11 November, would ban ten manipulative online design 'traps' (from cancellation harder than signup to fake notifications) and, for the first time in EU consumer law, set rules for AI shopping agents: users choose which purchases need their approval, and agents must disclose sponsored suggestions. Fines could reach 6% of global turnover; Germany prefers amending existing directives.
candidates.why_it_matters: Europe writing the mandate of a consumer's agent into law: which purchases it may make alone, and that it must say when it is paid to suggest. The same questions OpenAI answered by platform rule yesterday, now by regulation.
claims_to_check: The Commission's own proposal once presented today: the final text may differ from the leaked draft
The 12-month application period and the 6% fines, at the proposal

importance.reason: EU regulation of AI agents, presented today; the agentic edition's regulatory story of the week.

candidates.title: Defined.ai opens its AI training-data marketplace to partners at Web Summit, after cutting 30% of its staff
candidates.summary: At Web Summit on 10 November, Defined.ai's founder and CEO Daniela Braga presented its data marketplace, a strategic access programme and a partnership model; she said over 280 companies joined the partner programme in two weeks, the company holds over 10 petabytes and 2,000 datasets, and data is now 70% of its revenue. She also said the company cut about 30% of its staff this year, mainly in Europe, as the market slowed.
candidates.why_it_matters: A Portuguese AI company selling the data that frontier labs train on, with demand moving to physical tasks; and an honest read of the market cycle from inside the summit.
claims_to_check: All figures are the company's, as told to Tek: 280 partners, 10 PB, 2,000 datasets, 70% of revenue, 30% staff cut

importance.reason: Portugal's best-known AI company at the summit; context more than breaking news.
